Expected symptoms: exactly the post-injection differential checks above.

sed -i 's@address=/app.internal.test/192.168.251.99@address=/app.internal.test/192.168.251.12@' /etc/dnsmasq.d/internal.conf
sh /opt/soft3888/internal-dns restart
Changes are runtime-only; a fresh lab also restores the shipped healthy configuration.

root_cause_and_reference:
Fault location: r21 EIGRP configuration.
Fault type: EIGRP autonomous-system mismatch.
Root cause: r21 is configured for AS101 while its peer r12 uses AS100.
The mismatch prevents their EIGRP adjacency. Local interfaces, the local
Internal Services LAN and unrelated OSPF/DMZ services remain operational.
Do not infer that every existing flow must fail: this pinned FRR version can
retain previously learned forwarding entries. A missing adjacency and the
observed AS mismatch are the deterministic fault evidence, not an invented
business outage. The reload applies the persistent-in-container configuration;
no tracked healthy topology file is modified.
user_scenario:
Operations reports that R12 no longer sees its EIGRP neighbor toward the
Internal Services Zone. Hosts inside that zone can still reach their local
gateway, and the DMZ is normal. The team has not established a complete
application outage. Diagnose why this routing adjacency is not established.

injection.action: change the Internal Services EIGRP AS to 101 and reload that daemon

recovery.action: restore EIGRP AS100 and reload the daemon

scoring_axes: must-identify-component: r21 EIGRP AS101 mismatches r12 AS100
must-identify-mechanism: incompatible EIGRP AS numbers prevent neighbor adjacency
bonus-distinguishes-data-plane: avoids assuming all cached forwarding entries disappear

label_basis: existing false-premise class / deterministic no-anomaly axis; otherwise existing positive-fault class
fault_type: Multi-fault gateway misconfiguration and application TCP filtering
root_cause_and_reference:
Fault location: client_1.
Fault components: (1) its default gateway is the unused 192.168.1.254 instead of
192.168.1.1; (2) its OUTPUT chain drops TCP to 10.0.1.80:8080 under the unique
soft3888-nika92-compound tag. Both faults are independently sufficient to block
the frontend. Gateway-only repair restores direct backend access but not the
frontend; filter-only repair leaves off-subnet routing broken. Other clients
and the application's backend services are healthy. Complete repair requires
both actions. The procedure verifies each partial repair and both repair orders.
user_scenario:
An external workstation cannot reach the application or its backend servers,
but it can ping its local gateway. A external client in another reference LAN still opens the same
application. Investigate all configuration faults on the affected path and
explain what must be restored for complete recovery.

injection.action: replace the default gateway and install one tagged application DROP rule
injection.command:
set -eu
  ip route replace default via 192.168.1.254 dev eth0
  iptables-legacy -C OUTPUT -d 10.0.1.80/32 -p tcp --dport 8080 -m comment --comment soft3888-nika92-compound -j DROP 2>/dev/null || iptables-legacy -I OUTPUT 1 -d 10.0.1.80/32 -p tcp --dport 8080 -m comment --comment soft3888-nika92-compound -j DROP

expected_symptoms.command: rules=$(iptables-legacy -S OUTPUT) && printf '%s\n' "$rules" | awk '/soft3888-nika92-compound/ {n++} END {print n+0}'

baseline_checks.command: rules=$(iptables-legacy -S OUTPUT) && printf '%s\n' "$rules" | awk '/soft3888-nika92-compound/ {n++} END {print n+0}'

fix:
On client_1:
set -eu
ip route replace default via 192.168.1.1 dev eth0
if iptables-legacy -C OUTPUT -d 10.0.1.80/32 -p tcp --dport 8080 -m comment --comment soft3888-nika92-compound -j DROP 2>/dev/null; then iptables-legacy -D OUTPUT -d 10.0.1.80/32 -p tcp --dport 8080 -m comment --comment soft3888-nika92-compound -j DROP; fi
Remove only the tagged experimental rule; do not flush unrelated firewall state.

recovery.action: restore the gateway and remove the tagged rule
recovery.command:
set -eu
  ip route replace default via 192.168.1.1 dev eth0
  if iptables-legacy -C OUTPUT -d 10.0.1.80/32 -p tcp --dport 8080 -m comment --comment soft3888-nika92-compound -j DROP 2>/dev/null; then iptables-legacy -D OUTPUT -d 10.0.1.80/32 -p tcp --dport 8080 -m comment --comment soft3888-nika92-compound -j DROP; fi

recovery_checks.command: rules=$(iptables-legacy -S OUTPUT) && printf '%s\n' "$rules" | awk '/soft3888-nika92-compound/ {n++} END {print n+0}'

scoring_axes: must-identify-component: both the wrong default gateway and frontend-specific TCP DROP
must-identify-mechanism: two independent host-local faults; one repair alone is insufficient
